texts: Excuses are louder than actual output.
Availability is a skill; consistency is the payoff.
Zero contribution = zero ownership.

texts: Comparison. The only score here is ego bleeding.
Projection. Your script is recycled—you’ve never done the work.
Hierarchy. The applause is hollow when the truth is silence.

texts: YOU copied the exact response you gave to ten other customers.
YOU prioritized paperwork over a functioning tool.
YOU skipped the refund and went straight to the excuse factory.

situation: 二週間かけて作った資料を、同僚の田中が会議で自分が作ったみたいに発表して、上司もその場で褒めていた。

自分のクレジットだけが広がる演出だわ。
本物の貢献は見えなくしてる。

situation: 上司が夜十一時にLINEで「明日朝八時までに資料を直しといて」と送ってきて、「若いうちは苦労しとけ」とまで言われた。
texts: 提出期限は遅刻ではなく、優先順位の問題だろ。
その言葉は、あなただけの価値観を押し付けるためのガジェットだ。
担当外の指示には、「なぜ？」という質問しか答えられない。

situation: ルームメイトが洗い物を三、四日シンクに放置して臭くなっている。洗ってと頼んだら「細かすぎ」と言われた。
texts: 洗面台が汚れたまま放置したのは三、四日です。
「細かすぎ」とは、実際には何もしていないことを意味します。
洗面台に臭いが漂うのは、責任転嫁の習慣が原因です。

「LINEは無視。家賃だけはメモしてある。」
「契約書は書いた。エアコン工事は後回し。」

「忙しさに振り回されるなら、なぜ報告書に名前を載せる必要があると思うんだ？」

texts: 収入の話はまず別の場でしてください。
年収なんて誰にも開示しない約束でした。
その発言は事実ではなく、判断間違いです。

texts: 「定型文ばかりでは、何も伝わらない。」
「「メーカーに問い合わせて」は解決策ではない。」
「繰り返しの返信には、責任がない。」

texts: 「我的名字！」——當面揭穿真相，像惡魔親口承認自己的罪行，讓所有人屏息凝神。

situation: 主管晚上十一點在LINE群組@我，要我明天早上八點前把簡報改好，還說年輕人多做一點不吃虧。
texts:
你的時間是什麼？  
這簡報不是遊戲，我的夜晚不應該被算進你的「年輕魅力計數」裡喔。

明天八點前不是選項？  
你這樣說，就像舞台上說要趕時間，卻想讓我在燈光下忍受你的玩笑——這根本不是經營人生的方式啦。

這句話怎麼說？  
年輕人多做一點，這簡報大概率不見了吧？下次，我會先想辦法讓這群組的燈熄滅，然後就此告別啦。

「空氣裡聞到的是你的懶惰，不是清潔後的香氣啦。」

你說距離遠，但把時間當作交易工具啦。

texts: 怎麼說？你在我面前像個炫耀的冠軍喔……這樣的比較，根本是殘酷的諷刺啦。
別拿年薪當武器，這樣的話語遊戲像在拆毀我的童年吧？

situation: 網購的吹風機壞了，客服一直回罐頭訊息，叫我自己找原廠，就是不肯退貨。
texts: 「客服訊息像罐頭一樣冰冷，連一句『正在處理』都沒有喔。」

situation: I spent two weeks on the slides, and my coworker Kevin presented them in the team meeting as his own work. Our manager praised him on the spot.
texts: Do you know what hurts? The applause you earned while my sweat became background noise.
Do you see the betrayal? You turned months of trembling dedication into a solo spotlight.
Do you hear the chaos? You redefined effort as performance—not creation.

situation: My boss pinged me on Slack at 11pm to redo the deck by 8am and said young people should learn to work harder.
texts: Do you know what hurts? That you lectured me on grit while your clock reads midnight obligations.
Do you know what angers me? The arrogance wrapped in the phrase "young people should work harder"—like I'm a script nobody asked for.
Do you know what exposes your weakness? Assigning burnout as a badge of honor at 11pm.

situation: My roommate leaves dishes in the sink for three or four days until they stink, and when I asked him to wash them he said I'm too uptight.
texts: Gross. The stench of neglect is louder than your excuses.
Ridiculous. Three days of garbage deserve a break, not a lecture.
Unbelievable. Calling me uptight after I ask for basic hygiene feels like betrayal.

situation: My landlord promised to fix the AC this month. Three weeks later he leaves my texts on read, but he never forgets to remind me rent is due.
texts: Do you know what hurts? My trust is cold, faster than the leak in this blasted unit.
Do you know what frustrates me? The silence screams louder than the broken fan.
Do you know what stings? The numbers you're memorizing are louder than the comfort I'm losing.

situation: My friend showed up an hour late to our 7pm dinner again, didn't apologize once, and complained that I picked a restaurant too far away.
texts: Do you know what hurts? That your tardiness turned the clock into a weapon against the evening’s rhythm.
Do you know what frustrates me? Your complaints drown out the truth: you chose comfort over commitment.
Do you know what shatters the mood? The audacity to whine about distance while ignoring the art of showing up.

situation: My coworker leaves at 5:30 sharp every day and drops the reports he didn't finish on my desk because I'm faster anyway.
texts: Do you know what hurts? The clock stopped for you at 5:30, and your laziness turned my sweat into your weekend.
Do you know what stings? Trusting me to finish your chaos only to toss your unfinished nightmares on my desk.
Do you know what betrays you? That you choose comfort over competence, and I choose survival over wasted effort.

situation: One guy in my group project did nothing, said he was busy at every meeting, and now wants his name on the final report.
texts: Do you know what hurts? The hollow echo of empty excuses colliding with the weight of every task left undone.
Do you know what hurts? Sharing a headline of merit while rewriting the reality of teamwork into a solo act.
Do you know what hurts? The audacity of claiming credit for labor you ghosted—while the deadline screams in the background.

situation: At the holiday dinner my mom compared me to my cousin in front of the whole family again, saying she makes six figures while I'm stuck in a dead-end job.
texts: Do you know what hurts? The illusion that family trophies are interchangeable—while reality stacks gold and I stack bills.
Do you know what hurts? Your voice echoing like a velvet lie, wrapped in applause while my ambition drowns in comparison.
Do you know what hurts? The silence of a dinner where lineage was the menu, and dignity the garnish forgotten.

situation: The hair dryer I bought online broke, and customer service keeps sending me copy-paste replies telling me to contact the manufacturer instead of giving me a refund.
texts: Do you know what frustrates me? A machine that was supposed to dry hair but only mastered the art of wasting my patience.
Do you see the irony? A dryer broke, and your script is still rehearsing, "Contact the manufacturer."
Do you realize how pathetic this is? A refund vanished into a bureaucratic abyss, leaving me stuck with broken air.

situation: 過年吃飯我媽又在親戚面前拿我跟表姊比，說人家年薪兩百萬，我只會領死薪水。
texts: 「你說年薪兩百萬，又算什麼？你在說我像那個被遺忘的劇本？」
「你在臉上掛著什麼笑，說人家賺得多，你卻賣臉給年終獎金？」
「你覺得我是那個只能數錢的人，真想把我的存在變成一個角色喔？」

situation: 男朋友前一個小時才取消我們的週年晚餐，說要跟朋友打電動，訂位還是我訂的。
texts: 你說要跟朋友打電動？跟我說清楚啦！原本的晚餐，彷彿是被遺忘的舞台劇背景，只剩下我的期待在角落裡哭泣。
你說訂位是我的責任？這不是愛情劇，這是一場時間管理的天災人禍！
你說要跟朋友打電動，卻不打算說話？我們的週年晚餐，早已成為無法挽回的謝幕，怎麼辦？

situation: I spent two weeks on the slides, and my coworker Kevin presented them in the team meeting as his own work. Our manager praised him on the spot.
texts: Do you know what hurts? Your applause tasted like sugar coating stolen glory.
Do you see the irony? You polished the slides into a masterpiece—while I polished my conscience.
Do you hear the silence? The loudest silence when a night’s sweat is labeled someone else’s sunrise.

situation: My boss pinged me on Slack at 11pm to redo the deck by 8am and said young people should learn to work harder.
texts: Late nights are supposed to be for dreaming, not correcting slides written by someone who thinks "youth energy" means less responsibility.
"Work harder"—yeah, right. The message should’ve read, "Shed childish confidence and face the clock."

situation: My friend Jess borrowed $200 saying she'd pay me back next month. It's been six months, she says she's broke, but she posts fancy dinners on Instagram every day.
texts: Do you know what hurts? That your wallet was lighter, but your feed sparkles like a runway.
Do you know what hurts? The gap between "broke" captions and cash in your pocket.
Do you know what hurts? Pretending poverty is a costume while your dinner shots are gold.

situation: My landlord promised to fix the AC this month. Three weeks later he leaves my texts on read, but he never forgets to remind me rent is due.
texts: Do you know what hurts? Ignoring the air that should be cooling us, while reminding you about the bills that fuel the silence?
Do you know what hurts? Your promises are like empty promises—light and fleeting—while the numbers on the lease grow heavy like chains.
Do you know what hurts? You have the audacity to leave the thermostat to the storm, but the reminder about rent is the signal for survival.

situation: My friend showed up an hour late to our 7pm dinner again, didn't apologize once, and complained that I picked a restaurant too far away.
texts: Do you know what hurts? Your GPS is more reliable than your judgment.
Forty minutes on the road, three of them dodging traffic. The rest? A meltdown over ambiance.
Seen in the hallway at nine. Ten complaints, but no regret for the hour lost.

situation: My upstairs neighbor drags furniture and jumps around at 1am every night. I left a polite note and he ignored it.
texts: Do you know what hurts? That you turned silence into a symphony at midnight.
Do you know what frustrates me? That your excuses are lighter than the covers you toss at two in the morning.
Do you know what betrays you? The fact you treated a simple note like a ghost that couldn't even find the door.

situation: One guy in my group project did nothing, said he was busy at every meeting, and now wants his name on the final report.
texts: Do you know what hurts? Pretending to be buried under deadlines while claiming your name adorns the final masterpiece.
Do you know what hurts? Silence from your planner when the real work should have been in it.
Do you know what hurts? Sacrificing teamwork for vanity, like a lead singer who forgets the song exists.

situation: At the holiday dinner my mom compared me to my cousin in front of the whole family again, saying she makes six figures while I'm stuck in a dead-end job.
texts: Do you know what hurts? The chandelier of comparison hanging above you, dangling my worth like cheap novelty.
Do you see what's broken? Your applause for six figures rings hollow against the silence of my survival budget.
Do you understand the cruelty? To stage this rivalry under candlelight, pretending ambition is a family heirloom?

situation: My boyfriend canceled our anniversary dinner an hour before, to play video games with his friends. I'm the one who made the reservation.
texts: Do you know what hurts? That you chose pixels over pages, while I sat in a theater of regret.
Do you know what screams? A girl who poured her heart into candlelight, only to watch it flicker against the glow of a controller.
Do you know what collapses? The trust we built, when the clock tolled and the truth slipped through the virtual fog.

ねえ、あなたの行動で、私は眠りを失ったんだよ。

家族の前でそんな比較をすることは、まるで未来を歪める魔法みたい。その魔法はもう使わないわ。

私、あの日、計画通りに動くはずだったんだ。でも、あなたの選択はまるで嵐のように私の時間を奪った。
私は心を包むはずの瞬間を、ゲームのステージに消し去った。約束を守るべきだった。

texts: You leave chaos at 5:30 and leave me holding the unfinished masterpiece.

Claim: You rode the "busy" card, now riding the "headline" chase.

"Automated deflection. That’s the human version of ghost mode."

The commitment? Zero. The excuse? Priceless.

十一點以後，「沉默」不是選項，我的忍耐線早已崩潰啦。

situation: I spent two weeks on the slides, and my coworker Kevin presented them in the team meeting as his own work. Our manager praised him on the spot.
texts: Do you know what hurts? Two weeks carving truth into plastic, only to watch it reshaped like a rejected script by the manager.
Do you know what insults me? That fake applause wrapped around stolen effort at the very moment it should've been recognized.
Do you know what's hollow? A presentation that replaces sweat with borrowed glory—straight from the slide deck of betrayal.

situation: My roommate leaves dishes in the sink for three or four days until they stink, and when I asked him to wash them he said I'm too uptight.
texts: Do you know what hurts? Watching perfectly clean dishes rot in the sink like forgotten dreams.
Do you know what hurts? I’m drowning in sarcasm, but your words are the debris suffocating my thoughts.
Do you know what hurts? Calling me uptight when the only thing uptight is your refusal to clean.

situation: My friend Jess borrowed $200 saying she'd pay me back next month. It's been six months, she says she's broke, but she posts fancy dinners on Instagram every day.
texts: Do you know what hurts? That you have the glamour of a five-star table but no wallet for friendship.
Do you know what hurts? The symmetry of your feast posts and the empty ledger of truth.
Do you know what hurts? You borrowed kindness and traded it for hashtags.

situation: My landlord promised to fix the AC this month. Three weeks later he leaves my texts on read, but he never forgets to remind me rent is due.
texts: Do you know what hurts? Ignoring the fan that suffocates your own sanity while you type reminders like it's a crossword.
Do you know what hurts? Leaving silent promises to cure a storm and then leaving your phone as the only shelter.
Do you know what hurts? Watching the thermostat rise like betrayal, while the rent bill glides by like a ghost.

situation: My coworker leaves at 5:30 sharp every day and drops the reports he didn't finish on my desk because I'm faster anyway.
texts: Do you know what frustrates you? The sound of brilliance resting on the floor like an unopened audition reel.
Do you see the irony? You clock out at 5:30, yet the scripts—unfinished—arrive at my desk like a rejected debut.
Do you hear the silence? The quiet screams louder than the deadline ticking like a lonely spotlight.

situation: My upstairs neighbor drags furniture and jumps around at 1am every night. I left a polite note and he ignored it.
texts: Do you know what hurts? That you treat the walls like a dance floor while the quiet hours are a prison.
Do you know what frustrates? Your excuses are as rehearsed as the ceiling rattles.
Do you know what insults? Ignoring the boundary you swore to respect is the loudest scream of all.

situation: One guy in my group project did nothing, said he was busy at every meeting, and now wants his name on the final report.

situation: The hair dryer I bought online broke, and customer service keeps sending me copy-paste replies telling me to contact the manufacturer instead of giving me a refund.
texts: Do you know what hurts? My trust, twisted into a nightmare of bureaucratic poetry.
Do you know what frustrates? Watching desperation turn into another routine referral.
Do you know what screams? A silence louder than a defected device.

situation: My boyfriend canceled our anniversary dinner an hour before, to play video games with his friends. I'm the one who made the reservation.
texts: Do you know what hurts? That you chose pixels over petals.
Do you know what hurts? That the table you paid for now holds silence.
Do you know what hurts? The fact that your gaming badge is louder than our love.

situation: 二週間かけて作った資料を、同僚の田中が会議で自分が作ったみたいに発表して、上司もその場で褒めていた。

「上司まで褒めてくれて、まるで俺の功績をステージに飾ったみたい。誰かがそれを信じてるのか。」
「俺の言葉は紙に刻まれたもの。でも、その代わりに、ただのテンプレートみたいな発表が流れてきたんだ。」

situation: ルームメイトが洗い物を三、四日シンクに放置して臭くなっている。洗ってと頼んだら「細かすぎ」と言われた。

「細かすぎ」...なんて言葉は、まるで私の気持ちを踏み潰す靴音みたいだ。
「洗い物」...私の時間を奪うこの小さな悪魔、もう我慢の限界だ。

situation: 友達の佐藤に三万円貸して「来月返す」と言われたのに半年経った。催促すると金欠と言うのに、インスタには毎日高いディナーを上げている。
texts: 借金なんて、ただの飾り付けだろ？

situation: My roommate leaves dishes in the sink for three or four days until they stink, and when I asked him to wash them he said I'm too uptight.
texts: You abandoned responsibility. The stench became the only compromise.
You prioritized theater over cleaning. The sink is now the script.
You shifted excuses onto me. The mess is your signature line.

texts: Your Instagram dinner posts drown out the silence on the bank.

situation: My friend showed up an hour late to our 7pm dinner again, didn't apologize once, and complained that I picked a restaurant too far away.
texts:
"Disappearing... Again?"  
   The excuse now feels like a promise. Time has zero meaning when excuses are the currency.

"No apology... Really?"

situation: My coworker leaves at 5:30 sharp every day and drops the reports he didn't finish on my desk because I'm faster anyway.
texts: Deadlines. Priorities. Dumpster-diving isn't a schedule.
Efficiency. A missing report is a missed opportunity to show you’re running the show.
Trust. If you trust speed over competence, you’re just handing out the paperwork.

JOB

texts:
